title: Free LLM APIs for Indian Developers: Regional & Global Picks
description: Free LLM APIs for Indian developers in 2026: Sarvam, Krutrim, AI4Bharat and BharatGen vs Gemini and Groq, with Hindi code, INR payments and DPDP notes.
author: freellm.site
content:
For most Indian developers, the best free LLM API right now is **Google Gemini's free tier** for general work, since it needs no card and includes current Flash models. **Sarvam AI** is the best free option for Indian languages: every new account gets ₹100 of credits that never expire. Its flagship `sarvam-105b` model supports the 10 most-spoken Indian languages through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Add **Groq** or **Mistral** as a no-card fallback and you have a working stack without entering a card.

All free tiers, credits and limits below were checked against each provider's official site or docs on 29 September 2026. Where we couldn't confirm a free offer, we say so rather than guess.

## What are the best free LLM APIs for Indian developers?

The short list is two Indian providers for Indic-language work and two or three global free tiers for everything else. Indian providers mostly give you starter credits billed in rupees, not permanent free tiers. The global providers give you permanent free tiers with rate limits but charge in US dollars once you upgrade.

| Provider | Free offer (verified 29 Sep 2026) | Card needed? | Indic languages | OpenAI-compatible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Sarvam AI](/providers/sarvam_ai/) | ₹100 signup credits, never expire | No card mentioned in docs | 10 Indian languages + English (chat); 22 for speech/translation | Yes (`/v1`) |
| [Krutrim AI](/providers/krutrim/) | No signup credit amount published | Prepaid top-up, min ₹1,500 incl. GST (UPI or card) | Krutrim models; see below | Yes (`/v1`) |
| [AI4Bharat](/providers/ai4bharat/) | Open weights (e.g. IndicTrans2, MIT) | No (self-host) | All 22 scheduled languages (translation) | No hosted API |
| [BharatGen](/providers/bharatgen/) | Open weights (Param2, non-commercial licence) | No (self-host) | English + all 22 scheduled languages | No hosted API |
| [Google Gemini](/providers/google_gemini/) | Permanent free tier on Flash / Flash-Lite models | No | Multilingual (not India-specific) | Yes (`/v1beta/openai/`) |
| [Groq](/providers/groq/) | Permanent free plan, e.g. gpt-oss-120b at 30 RPM / 1K RPD | No (card only to upgrade) | Multilingual (not India-specific) | Yes |
| [Mistral AI](/providers/mistral/) | Free mode, "no credit card required" | No | Multilingual (not India-specific) | Yes |
| [OpenRouter](/providers/openrouter/) | `:free` models, 20 RPM / 50 RPD | No for free models | Depends on model | Yes |

Two big changes since our earlier version of this post: **GitHub Models was fully retired on 30 July 2026**, and **Cerebras no longer has a permanently free tier**. Its free trial is now $5 of credits that expire after 30 days and needs a verified payment method. Neither is a good no-card starting point for Indian developers anymore.

## Which Indian LLM providers offer free API access?

Only **Sarvam AI** has a documented, self-serve free allowance for a hosted LLM API today. **Krutrim** runs a hosted, OpenAI-compatible API, but its docs don't state a signup credit amount. **AI4Bharat** and **BharatGen** publish open-weight models you can download and run yourself, but neither offers a hosted chat API.

### Sarvam AI

Sarvam is the most practical Indian choice for a free LLM API. Its [credits and rate limits page](https://docs.sarvam.ai/api/getting-started/ratelimits) says: "Sarvam offers **₹100 worth of free credits** for every user on signup". The credits work across every Sarvam API and never expire. The marketing pricing page only says "Start with free credits" without naming a figure. We're using the ₹100 in the docs.

- **Chat models:** `sarvam-105b` (128K context) and `sarvam-105b-conversations` (32K context, tuned for chatbots and voice agents). The older Sarvam-M has been deprecated.
- **Indic coverage:** the 105B chat model is trained on "native script, romanized, and code-mixed" input in the **10 most-spoken Indian languages plus English**. The speech-to-text and document models cover **22 Indian languages plus English**.
- **Price after credits:** ₹29.28 per 1M input tokens and ₹73.20 per 1M output tokens for Sarvam 105B, billed in rupees. So ₹100 goes a fair way for testing.
- **Free-tier rate limits (Starter):** 60 requests/minute for chat by default, 40 requests/minute for `sarvam-105b`.
- **Signup:** create an account on the [Sarvam dashboard](https://dashboard.sarvam.ai) and generate a key. Sarvam's docs don't mention any PAN, GST or phone-verification requirement for signup. If one appears at signup, it isn't documented.

The endpoint is OpenAI-compatible (`https://api.sarvam.ai/v1`), so the standard OpenAI SDK works. There's a Hindi example below. Sarvam also serves open-weight models on its `/v2` route (GLM-5.3, Gemma 4 31B, DeepSeek V4 Flash), but these are in beta. Your key has to be whitelisted before they respond.

### Krutrim AI (Ola)

Krutrim Cloud is a full Indian cloud (GPUs, Kubernetes, storage) with an **AI Studio** model-as-a-service layer. Its inference API is OpenAI-compatible at `https://cloud.olakrutrim.com/v1`, and the docs show the OpenAI Python SDK with the `krutrim-1` model.

We **couldn't confirm a free LLM allowance**. The AI Studio page says "No credit card required" to get started. But the [Krutrim Cloud docs](https://docs.cloud.olakrutrim.com/) don't publish a signup credit amount. The billing docs mention "offer credits" with expiry dates without saying who gets them or how many. The docs do spell out the paid path:

- **Signup** needs your full name, email and **mobile number**, with OTP verification on both phone and email. You choose an Individual or Organization account. The docs also warn that names must match official documents because the platform "will soon introduce identity verification" for new and existing accounts.
- **Payment** is prepaid. Top-ups are via **UPI or card** (through Razorpay), the minimum top-up is **₹1,500 including GST**, and **18% GST** is added on top.
- **Krutrim's own models** are priced at ₹16.6 per 1M tokens (Krutrim-1) and ₹6.6 per 1M tokens (Krutrim-2) in the docs' model price table. It also hosts open models like DeepSeek-R1, Gemma and Llama.

If you want to pay in rupees through UPI with a GST invoice, Krutrim is the easiest paid option on this list. Treat it as a low-cost paid API, not a free one, until it publishes a free allowance.

### AI4Bharat (IIT Madras)

[AI4Bharat](https://ai4bharat.iitm.ac.in/) is a research lab. It releases open models, not a hosted API. Its main releases are IndicTrans2 for translation across all 22 scheduled languages, IndicBERT, IndicXlit for transliteration, Indic ASR/TTS models and the Airavata LLM. For example, `ai4bharat/indictrans2-en-indic-1B` on Hugging Face is **MIT-licensed**. It's gated, but approval is automatic.

AI4Bharat is free in the open-source sense. You download the weights and run them on your own GPU, or on a GPU cloud like Krutrim or [Neysa](/providers/neysa_ai/).

### BharatGen (IIT Bombay consortium)

[BharatGen](https://bharatgen.com/) is the government-backed "sovereign AI" initiative. Its newest text model, **Param2** (17B-parameter MoE, 2.4B active per token, 32K context), covers **English plus all 22 scheduled Indian languages**. It supports reasoning, tool calling and code generation. The weights are on Hugging Face under the `bharatgenai` organisation. There's also the Param1 family (English and Hindi) and domain models such as AgriParam, FinanceParam, LegalParam and AyurParam.

Two things to know. First, Param2's model card lists a **BharatGen Non-Commercial licence**, so check it before you ship a product. Second, we found **no public hosted API**, so you self-host. The old `bharatgen.iitb.ac.in` address listed in many directories no longer resolves. The official site is now bharatgen.com.

### Other Indian providers

We checked the rest of the Indian providers in our directory and couldn't confirm a self-serve free LLM API for any of them:

- **[CoRover BharatGPT](/providers/corover_bharatgpt/):** enterprise conversational AI platform, sold through "Get a Demo".
- **[Gnani.ai](/providers/gnani_ai/):** has self-serve API signup, but for **voice** (speech-to-text, text-to-speech, voice agents), not a general chat LLM.
- **[Soket AI](/providers/soket_ai/):** publishes the open-source **Pragna-1B** model (Hindi, Gujarati, Bangla, English). No hosted API is advertised.
- **[Neysa AI](/providers/neysa_ai/):** a GPU and AI cloud (Velocis). Useful for self-hosting AI4Bharat or BharatGen models. Pricing goes through sales.
- **Hanooman AI:** its site loads but shows no readable API or pricing information, so we couldn't verify any free API access.

## Which global free LLM APIs work best from India?

**Gemini, Groq and Mistral** are the strongest global options. All three have permanent free tiers that need no card, which matters in India because many debit cards and RuPay cards fail on foreign billing. **OpenRouter's** free models are a useful fourth option for trying many models behind one key.

### Google Gemini

India is on Gemini API's list of available regions, and the free tier needs only a Google account. According to the [official pricing page](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing), current Flash-class models are "Free of charge" on the free tier. That includes Gemini 3.8 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, 3.1 Flash-Lite and 2.5 Flash, as well as 2.5 Pro. The newer Pro previews (such as 3.1 Pro Preview) are paid-only. Google no longer publishes fixed free-tier numbers in its docs. Your limits are shown in AI Studio.

One catch matters for Indian apps handling user data: the pricing page's "Used to improve our products" row says **Yes** for the free tier and **No** for paid. Don't send personal data from real users through the free tier. There's more on this in the DPDP section.

Gemini also has an OpenAI-compatible endpoint at `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/`, so it slots into the same code as everything else here.

### Groq

Groq's free plan needs no payment method. Its [rate limits page](https://console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits) lists free-plan limits of **30 requests/minute, 1,000 requests/day, 8K tokens/minute and 200K tokens/day** for `openai/gpt-oss-120b`, `openai/gpt-oss-20b` and `qwen/qwen3.8-27b`. Llama 3.3 70B, which older guides call "free on Groq", is no longer on the free-plan table.

The payment catch: Groq's billing FAQ says upgrading needs "a valid payment method (credit card, US bank account, or SEPA debit account)". There's no UPI or INR option, so stay on the free plan unless you have an international card.

### Mistral AI

Mistral's docs say its Studio free mode is enabled by default "with no credit card required", with usage and rate limits applied. It's a good third fallback.

### OpenRouter

OpenRouter's free model variants (IDs ending in `:free`) are limited to **20 requests/minute and 50 requests/day**. That rises to 1,000/day once you've bought at least 10 credits in total. See our [rate limits comparison](/blog/free-llm-api-rate-limits-compared/) for how these caps compare across providers.

## What about latency and payments from India?

**Latency:** none of the global free tiers let you pick an Indian serving region, and none publish where free-tier requests are served. Sarvam says its platform is "developed and operated entirely in India". Krutrim says it deploys models on domestic servers. That's the best case for low latency from Indian cities, but we didn't benchmark it. Time a few requests from your own server region before you commit.

**Payments:** for a developer paying with Indian cards or UPI, the providers rank like this, from least to most friction:

1. **No payment at all:** Gemini free tier, Groq free plan, Mistral free mode, OpenRouter `:free` models, Sarvam's ₹100 credits.
2. **INR billing:** Sarvam (prices in ₹) and Krutrim (UPI or card, 18% GST, ₹1,500 minimum top-up).
3. **USD billing with an international card:** Groq Developer tier, Cerebras (card needed even for its trial), most other global paid tiers.

When you outgrow the free tiers, our guide to the [cheapest LLM API after the free tier](/blog/cheapest-llm-api-after-free-tier/) shows how to compare paid options on your real token mix.

## How do you call an LLM in Hindi with an OpenAI-compatible API?

Use the standard OpenAI SDK and point `base_url` at Sarvam. Then fall back to Gemini's OpenAI-compatible endpoint if Sarvam errors out or your credits run out. Both base URLs and model IDs come from each provider's official docs.

```python
import os
from openai import OpenAI

PROVIDERS = [
    # Sarvam: Indic-first, ₹100 free credits on signup
    {"base_url": "https://api.sarvam.ai/v1",
     "api_key": os.environ.get("SARVAM_API_KEY"),
     "model": "sarvam-105b"},
    # Gemini: permanent free tier, no card
    {"base_url": "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/",
     "api_key": os.environ.get("GEMINI_API_KEY"),
     "model": "gemini-3.5-flash"},
]

messages = [
    {"role": "system",
     "content": "आप एक सहायक हैं। हमेशा सरल हिंदी में उत्तर दें।"},
    {"role": "user",
     "content": "UPI क्या है? तीन छोटे बिंदुओं में समझाइए।"},
]

for p in PROVIDERS:
    if not p["api_key"]:
        continue
    try:
        client = OpenAI(base_url=p["base_url"], api_key=p["api_key"])
        resp = client.chat.completions.create(
            model=p["model"], messages=messages, max_tokens=800
        )
        print(f"[{p['model']}]\n{resp.choices[0].message.content}")
        break
    except Exception as err:  # rate limit, no credits, outage
        print(f"{p['model']} failed: {err}; trying next provider")
```

A few tips for Indic prompts:

- **Write the system prompt in the target language**, or say explicitly "answer in Hindi (Devanagari script)". Otherwise many models drift back to English.
- **Hinglish works.** Sarvam's model is trained on romanized and code-mixed input, so `"UPI kya hai?"` is a valid prompt.
- **Budget more tokens.** Indic scripts usually tokenize into more tokens than the same sentence in English, so raise `max_tokens` and expect to use free quotas faster.
- **`sarvam-105b` is a reasoning model.** Its thinking tokens count toward `max_tokens`, so don't set the cap too low.

Our [OpenAI-compatible API guide](/blog/openai-compatible-api-guide/) explains why, and the [chatbot tutorial](/blog/free-llm-api-customer-support-chatbot/) shows the same fallback pattern in a full app.

## What does the DPDP Act mean for using these APIs?

If your app sends **personal data of users in India** to an LLM API, you're a Data Fiduciary under the [Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023](https://www.meity.gov.in/static/uploads/2024/06/2bf1f0e9f04e6fb4f8fef35e82c42aa5.pdf). The LLM provider is typically your Data Processor. The official texts say:

- **The Rules are notified.** MeitY notified the DPDP Rules, 2025 on 14 November 2025 with an **18-month phased compliance period** ([PIB release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2190014)).
- **Cross-border transfer isn't banned by default.** Section 16(1) of the Act lets the Central Government "by notification, restrict the transfer of personal data… to such country or territory outside India as may be so notified". Section 16(2) keeps any stricter sector-specific law in force. In practice, calling a US-hosted API is allowed unless the destination is notified, or a sector regulator (for example in finance) requires local storage.
- **Significant Data Fiduciaries have more duties.** Per MeitY's [summary of the Rules](https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/nov/doc20251117695301.pdf), they may have to follow government directions on restricted categories of data, "including local storage where needed".
- **Penalties are large.** They go up to ₹250 crore for failing to keep reasonable security safeguards, and up to ₹200 crore for breach-notification failures or violations involving children's data.

What this means for free tiers specifically:

- **Gemini's free tier uses your content to improve Google's products.** Keep real users' personal data off it. Use it for synthetic data, public content and prototypes.
- **Read each provider's data-use terms before sending anything personal.** A free tier's data terms often differ from the paid tier's.
- **If you need data kept in India**, Sarvam and Krutrim are the hosted options that say they operate in India. Self-hosting AI4Bharat or BharatGen weights on Indian infrastructure is the strictest option. Sarvam's privacy policy names Sarvam as a Data Fiduciary under the DPDPA, "notified under DPDPA Section 10" as a Significant Data Fiduciary.

This is a summary of public texts, not legal advice. For production apps handling Indian users' data, get a lawyer to review your processor contracts.

## Which setup should an Indian developer start with?

For a **general app or prototype**, start with the Gemini free tier and keep Groq as a fallback. Both are no-card, permanent and OpenAI-compatible. Our [no-credit-card API key guide](/blog/how-to-get-free-llm-api-key-no-credit-card/) walks through the signup.

For **Hindi, Tamil, Telugu or any other Indian-language product**, start with Sarvam's ₹100 credits, using `sarvam-105b` or `sarvam-105b-conversations` for chatbots. Then pay in rupees when you're ready. Krutrim is the alternative if you want UPI billing and a GST invoice from day one.

For **offline, research or data-sensitive work**, download AI4Bharat's IndicTrans2 (MIT) or BharatGen's Param2 (check the non-commercial licence) and run them on your own hardware or an Indian GPU cloud.
